toolLead: Open the PDF, prepare your signature and choose how to download it. A visible mark is optional when signing with a certificate.
legalBody: A drawn or typed signature is an image: it does not verify the signer's identity by itself. A certificate signature links the document to a key and lets a reader check for later changes. Acceptance depends on the recipient, certificate and applicable rules; PAdES format does not guarantee a qualified signature.
guide.visual.body1: Open the PDF and use the arrows to reach page 3, where the signature box appears. Create your signature, select “Use this signature” and add it to that page. Drag it into the box without covering any text. The first two pages need no extra mark if the recipient only asks you to sign at the end.
guide.visual.title2: Draw, type or choose an image
guide.visual.body2: Draw with a mouse or finger, type your name, or choose a PNG, JPEG or WebP image. A transparent PNG avoids covering the document. Typed names shrink to fit, including longer names. Check the mark before placing it: the same image is used for every position you add.
guide.visual.body3: Choose the visual download and open the result in a PDF reader. Check all three pages, the name and the position. If no signature is placed, the download is a copy of the original. An image adds no certificate or proof of identity; check that the recipient accepts this kind of signature.
guide.certificate.title1: Prepare the file and its password
guide.certificate.body1: The browser method needs a .p12 or .pfx containing an RSA private key and its matching certificate, plus the password. A public .cer file cannot replace it. The tool checks that the file opens, the key matches the certificate and the validity dates allow signing before it creates the signature.
guide.certificate.body2: To digitally sign a PDF with no previous signatures, select the certificate and sign without drawing anything. If you also want a visible mark, place it first. When the PDF already has digital signatures, the .p12 method stops; use AutoFirma without adding a new visible mark, then check all signatures in the result.
guide.certificate.title3: Verify the signature, not just the download
guide.certificate.body3: Open the signature panel in a compatible reader and check the signer, document integrity and certificate trust. This tool does not validate the trust chain or revocation status. The .p12 method adds neither an authority timestamp nor long-term validation data. Check the recipient's requirements before sending the document.
guide.placement.body1: In a three-page PDF, select page 3 and press “Add to this page” once. The signature appears only there. Drag it inside the paper to the reserved space, leaving room for the name and date added below it during export. The preview shows the signature image.
guide.placement.title2: The same signature on three pages
guide.placement.body2: “Add to all pages” creates a position on every page, even when you are only viewing one. Move each mark separately or remove it with the cross. Pressing the button again adds more positions: use the arrows to check for duplicates and to inspect pages with different sizes or margins.
guide.placement.title3: What the name and date mean
guide.placement.body3: The name is the text you enter; it is not checked against an identity. The date uses the device clock and selected language, and is not a certified timestamp. Characters from other writing systems are preserved; when browser rendering is needed, the line is stored as an image rather than selectable text.
guide.videoTitle: Place a signature on page three
guide.videoStep1: Open a three-page PDF and find the signature box on page 3.
guide.videoStep2: Prepare your signature and add it once to the selected page.
guide.videoStep3: Move the mark into the box without covering the document text.
guide.videoStep4: Download the visual copy and check all three pages before sending it.
